hints.title: Compare equal-sized blocks
hints.body: Write the first three terms as a,ar,ar2. The next three are r3 times these, so S6=(1+r3)S3.
hints.recap: Equal-length blocks of a geometric progression differ by a fixed power of the ratio.
hints.pitfall: The multiplier is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></math>, because corresponding terms are three positions apart.

recall.reminder: Equal-length blocks of a geometric progression differ by a fixed power of the ratio.

hints.title: Check cancellation, then find the ratio
hints.body: The seventh term is nonzero, so a≠0. Also 1+r+r2=(r+12)2+34>0, so S3=a(1+r+r2)≠0. Hence 1+r3=9.
hints.recap: Before dividing by an expression, establish that it is nonzero.
hints.pitfall: A formula containing <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> can introduce a spurious <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> case if its restriction is forgotten.
hints.pause: Solve the resulting cubic power equation for real <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>.

recall.reminder: Before dividing by an expression, establish that it is nonzero.

hints.title: Count the steps to the seventh term
hints.body: The seventh term is ar6=360. Substitute the ratio you found and solve for a.
hints.pitfall: The seventh term contains six multiplications by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></math>, not seven.
hints.pause: Find the first term and simplify the fraction.

solution:
The next block of three terms is r3 times the first block, so S6=(1+r3)S3. Since a≠0 and 1+r+r2>0, the first block sum is nonzero. Therefore 1+r3=9, so r=2.

The seventh term gives a26=360, hence a=360/64=45/8.

Answer E.
